title: Same-origin call
caption: The browser (or a wiki widget) calls /api/ang/712 on the site’s own host. There is no CORS and no API base URL in the frontend: a Vercel rewrite forwards the request — on staging to the context’s own function, on production to all, the whole API as one function. The rules are generated from the route table.

title: Identity and probes first
caption: H._handle stamps the clock and a request id — an incoming X-Request-Id or x-vercel-id is reused only if it is a plain token, otherwise a uuid4 — then answers /healthz (liveness) and /readyz (every table each enabled context declares is present) before anything else.

title: Two API surfaces, one body
caption: /api/v1/* has strict semantics: an unknown endpoint is 404 and every error is {code, message, request_id}. /api/* is the legacy surface whose responses are byte-pinned by the golden contract. Anything else is a static file, served from a realpath jail.

title: The dispatcher
caption: api() splits the path, ensures FTS5 is detected, and looks up (first segment, second segment) in ROUTES — 26 routes, each tagged with its bounded context. In split mode a route whose context is not enabled in this process is a 404: a service never answers for another.

title: The context reads SQLite
caption: The handler in sggs/reader.py runs parameterised SQL (never string-built; FTS columns allowlisted; every integer through _int()) on a connection opened read-only and immutable, one per handler thread. The app can never write to the scripture.

title: Respond: caching and headers
caption: Responses that depend only on the immutable database (ang, shabad, lines, analytics, timing …) are cacheable for the browser and the CDN, with a sha256 ETag that turns a repeat into a 304. Every response carries nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, no-referrer, HSTS, the request id and X-Service (which service answered).

title: Log the path, never the query
caption: One JSON line per request goes to stderr: method, path, status, milliseconds and the request id. The query string is never written, so what people search for is not recorded anywhere. The verbatim lines of Ang 712 reach the browser.

title: Errors and limits
caption: An ApiError keeps its status (a missing composition is 404); a bad parameter is 400 with a short message; anything unexpected is a generic 500 — the detail goes to the server log, never over the wire. The server caps handler threads and times out idle sockets so a slow client cannot hold a slot.
